rachel: FYI hitting an onboarding blocker: Node SDK treats embeddings.input as string only, but REST accepts `inputs` array. Also SDK's `truncate` default differs from docs.

tom: Which SDK version?

rachel: v0.8.2 in the sampleapp image. Quick repro: client.embeddings.create({model: 'text-embed-001', input: ['a','b'], truncate: 'end'}) -> client throws validation error. REST with same body returns both embeddings.

kevin: That mismatch explains the failing CI sampleapp smoke test. Two fixes: accept string|string[] for input; preserve enum strings for truncate (don't coerce to boolean).

rachel: Also noticed SDK lowercases enum and rejects `END`. Docs say case-insensitive. Onboarding note confused a few new users.

kevin: I'll open a patch: keep create() accepting single string for backcompat, and allow arrays. Update param validation and add unit + integration test against mock router.

ci-bot: Pipeline queued for branch sdk/embeddings-parity-fix (build #1432).

kevin: PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdk-node/pull/333 — fixes: accept array inputs, preserve truncate enum value, add tests, bump v0.8.3 -> v0.8.4.

rachel: Verified local sampleapp with the v0.8.4 build — batch embeds and docs behavior match REST now. Thanks!

kevin: Merged and published. Adding note in sampleapp README about minimum SDK version to avoid onboarding confusion.

rachel: Closing loop. If anyone sees more parity drift please add examples to #devex with repro steps. :pray:
